form.title: Zammad tickets
form.intro: McHarbor opens a Zammad ticket tagged mcharbor, adds internal notes on repeats and closes it when the alert recovers.
form.name: Channel name
form.instanceUrlHelp: Base URL of your Zammad, for example https://support.example.de. Only https:// is accepted.
form.accessTokenHelp: Personal access token of the McHarbor agent user, with the ticket.agent permission. Encrypted at rest.
form.groupHelp: Name of the Zammad group new tickets are created in. The token owner needs ticket.agent on it.
form.customerHelp: Login, email or guess:<email> of the customer user tickets are created for.
form.onBehalfOfHelp: Optional user id, login or email sent as the From header. Requires admin.user on the token owner.
form.ownerHelp: Optional login of the agent who owns new tickets. Leave blank to leave them unassigned.
form.resolveStateHelp: Zammad state set when the alert recovers, for example closed or pending close.
form.updateOnRepeatHelp: When an alert fires again while its ticket is open, add an internal note to it.
form.suppressNotifications: Suppress agent notifications for McHarbor notes
form.suppressNotificationsHelp: Ask Zammad not to notify agents about the notes and the close McHarbor adds.
form.statusMapHelp: Optional JSON object mapping custom Zammad states to open, acknowledged, resolved, closed or cancelled.
form.severityMapHelp: Optional JSON object mapping critical, warning and info to Zammad priority names. The default is 3 high, 2 normal and 1 low.
form.pollIntervalHelp: How often McHarbor reads the state of open tickets when no webhook is set up. 0 means webhook only.
form.reopenWindowHelp: When the alert fires again within this many minutes of the ticket being closed, McHarbor reopens that ticket instead of creating a new one. 0 always creates a new ticket.
form.secretKeep: Leave blank to keep the stored value.

guide.title: Connect Zammad
guide.step1: Create an agent user for McHarbor with the ticket.agent permission on the target group. Create a customer user (for example mcharbor@your-domain) that tickets are opened for.
guide.step2: Make sure Admin, Settings, System, API has token access enabled. Sign in as the McHarbor agent, open Profile, Token Access, and create a token with the ticket.agent permission.
guide.step3: Paste the Zammad URL, the token, the group name and the customer into this form, then click Test connection. McHarbor checks the token, the group and the customer, and creates nothing.
guide.step4: For status updates, save the channel and open it again. Under Ticket status from the ITSM, create the inbound URL and copy the URL and its signing secret; they are shown once.
guide.step5: In Zammad, open Admin, Webhook, and add a webhook with the inbound URL as the endpoint. Paste the signing secret into HMAC SHA1 Signature Token and keep SSL verification on.
guide.step6: Open Admin, Trigger, and add a trigger that activates on action, with the conditions Tags contains one mcharbor and State has changed, and the action Webhook set to the webhook above.
guide.step7: If you use a custom payload, include ticket id, number, title, state and owner login. Without a webhook, McHarbor polls open tickets at the poll interval.
